description:
This map displays false-colour infrared satellite imagery, presenting distinct land cover and habitat zones within a mountainous or high-altitude region. Healthy vegetation is represented in shades of red, while barren land, rocky outcrops, and sparse vegetation appear in blue-grey and brown tones. Water bodies are depicted in various shades of blue.

Four distinct areas are delineated by yellow boundaries and labelled with four-digit numerical codes:
- A large area on the upper left and central part of the image, prominently outlined in red, is labelled "4220" in yellow text. This zone exhibits strong red tones, indicating dense, healthy vegetation, consistent with classifications such as alpine grasslands or managed grasslands as referenced in the document context.
- Two areas on the right side and top right of the map, delineated by yellow lines, are labelled "5100" in yellow text. These areas show predominantly blue-grey and brown tones with scattered red, indicative of rocky or sparsely vegetated areas.
- A prominent dark blue water body, representing a river channel, is outlined in yellow and labelled "8110" in yellow text on a black background.
- A lighter blue, shallower water body or wide riverbed, also outlined in yellow, is labelled "6220" in yellow text on a light blue background.

No scale bar, compass rose, or detailed legend is provided within the image. The map illustrates different land cover types in a false-colour composite, likely for habitat classification or environmental monitoring purposes.
